auth.subtitle: Sign in to continue.

bx.artifacts.none: No firmware, CAD or other files yet.
bx.batch.hint: Makes the boxes and their labels at once: print the sheet, stick a label on each box. Name, contents and which box sits where come later, by scanning: on Scan → Intake, scan the cabinet, then the boxes that go into it.
bx.batch.label: Label
bx.delete.confirm: Delete the empty box “{name}”? Its files go with it.
bx.empty: Nothing in it yet. Check in a part by scanning its label or its barcode.
bx.f.name: Name
bx.f.title: Title (optional)
bx.hint: A box holds parts, assemblies and other boxes. Its large label opens its card on a phone: what is in it, check in and out, and its firmware, CAD and other files.
bx.in.box: The box is in this one now.
bx.in.elsewhere: That code belongs to another organisation.
bx.in.hint: Scan each part's small label or its own barcode; the camera stays on for the next one.
bx.in.self: A box cannot go inside itself.
bx.label: Print label
bx.move.hint: Scan the box it goes into, or say where it stands.
bx.move.notabox: That code is not a box of this organisation.
bx.out.done: Taken out: it is with you now.
bx.out.reserved: Taken out and reserved for the workspace.
edges.hint: Machines paired through the device flow (Link an edge). Each holds a device token that lets it work for its organisation, and nothing else.
edges.revoke.confirm: Revoke {name}? It must be paired again to upload.
edges.title: Edges
edges.tooold.title: Below the minimum edge version {min}: it must be updated.
guest.accounts.note: There is no sign-up. An organisation's admins invite the people they work with. If you were invited, use the temporary password from your invitation e-mail: you will be asked to choose a new one.
guest.tagline: Design, build and run hardware and software products, together.
help.edges.revoke: End this edge's access now. It has to be linked again to come back.
help.install.get: The installer and the package for this cloud's current edge, checked by SHA-256.
help.link.approve: Let this edge into the organisation you chose. It gets a token of its own, which you can revoke in Settings.
help.link.deny: Refuse this code. The edge is told, and nothing is stored.
help.signout: Sign out on this browser. Your workspaces stay as they are.
help.switch.off: Help on hover is off. Click to turn it back on.
help.switch.on: Help on hover is on: turn it off once you know the app.
hh.code.hint: Paste this code into “Create organisation” on the other site (for example prod after stage). Both then use the same ids for the organisation and its workspaces. Only share it with the operators of that site.
hh.email: e-mail (invited if they have no account)
hh.hint: Admins see every workspace of the organisation, manage who reads which, and link edges. A workspace's members see only that workspace.
hh.id: the organisation's id; names are only labels
hh.newspace.name: name of a new workspace
hh.renametenant: New name for the organisation (its id and every access stay the same)
hh.sharedspace: the shared workspace: everyone in the organisation reads it
hh.title: Organisation · {name}
home.active.hint: Used by an edge in the last {days} days.
home.active.none: No edge has used a workspace lately.
home.none: No workspaces you can open yet.
home.none.member: An admin of your organisation adds you to a workspace.
home.none.operator: As an operator, create the first organisation in
home.passive.hint: Not open on any edge lately. Their parts can be reused.
ib.adminonly: Only the organisation's admins check in, with two-step sign-in. You can describe and drop.
ib.done.box: Checked in: a new box in {place}.
ib.find: Search the stock, or type a new name
ib.knownMove: This label is {name}: checking in moves it into {place}.
ib.name: New article's name
ib.sayWhat: Say what it is: a device, a box of parts or loose parts.
in.atEdge: They wait in the intake: the edge's agent describes them, and an admin checks them in, on the edge or here.
in.hintLabel: Now scan the labels of what is here, one after the other.
in.hintPlace: Scan the shelf or box first: what you scan next goes into it.
in.needPhoto: A new article needs a photo first.
in.newHint: Take at least one photo (the label, the bag, the plate) and say in a few words what it is. The edge's agent makes the article from them; an admin checks it in.
in.newPlace: A blank label: name the shelf or box it is on.
in.notPlace: That label is on a part, not on a shelf or box. Scan the place first.
in.note: Note (what it is, what is in it)
in.noteNew: What is it? e.g. IKEA Ansulta USB cable, 2 m
in.pending: Scan the shelf or box first; {code} goes in then.
install.expires: The links work for 15 minutes; get new ones any time.
install.hint: An edge runs on a computer of the organisation and links to this site. What it keeps private stays on that computer.
install.manual.hint: The same by hand. Windows: venv\Scripts\python instead of venv/bin/python. The catalog then lives in the system's application-data folder.
install.sameplace: Keep both files in one folder: the installer checks the package against its SHA-256.
install.step.download: Download the installer and the package below, into the same folder.
install.step.first: On its first start the edge fetches what it still lacks; after linking, what its organisation already knows.
install.step.link: The edge opens on its local address. Then + Add connection, and approve its code on
install.step.python: The computer needs Python 3.10 or newer.
install.title: Install an edge on another computer
lb.hint: {n} labels. Print at actual size (100 %), never fit to page.
lb.smallbox: Small box, 38.1 × 21.2 mm (parts box, 65 a sheet)
lb.title: Labels
link.adminonly: Only an organisation's admins can link an edge.
link.approve.hint: Approve only if you started this pairing on that machine. An approved edge works for the organisation until you revoke it in Settings.
link.approved: Approved. The edge will finish linking within a few seconds.
link.askadmin: Ask an admin of your organisation to open this link.
link.code.hint: The code the edge shows. It is valid for 10 minutes.
link.denied: Denied. The edge has been told.
lq.printed.ask: Did every sheet print well? The queue is emptied, and the part of the last sheet that is left is remembered for the next print.
lq.summary: {sheets} sheets, {fill} % of the paper used; {left} mm left on the last sheet
lq.title: Print queue
lq.top: top of the first sheet already used
lq.usedArea: already used: put this sheet back in the printer, this part is skipped
mfa.again: Set up a new authenticator entry
mfa.againHint: Scan the new code and confirm one code from it: the new entry carries today's name ("maker5.cloud prod" or "… stage"), and the old entry stops working. Then delete the old entry in the app.
mfa.off: Two-step sign-in is off. It is optional for members and required for admins.
mfa.on: Two-step sign-in is on: each sign-in asks for a code from your authenticator app.
mfa.replaced: The new entry is in use. Delete the old one in your authenticator app.
mfa.required: You manage an organisation or the platform, so two-step sign-in is required. Set it up once with an authenticator app.
mfa.scan: Scan this with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password …), or type the key.
mfa.title: Two-step sign-in
mt.blank.hint: Print a sheet of codes before they belong to anything; stick one on a part and scan it to bind it. The smallest is 10 mm: enough for an SD or SIM card.
mt.f.name: Name, e.g. Raspberry Pi 1 Model B
mt.f.serial: Unit by unit (each its own code)
mt.hint: Everything this organisation keeps, in one catalogue: what is on hand, what workspaces reserved, what is free. Workspaces take parts in their Materials view; a label or tag opens a part's card.
mt.delete.ask: Delete {name}? Its {n} in stock, its codes and documents go with it. This cannot be undone.
mt.none: No articles yet. Add the first one.
mt.noworkspace: You are in no organisation yet. An admin adds you to one of its workspaces.
mt.proposed.accepted: Accepted: it is an article like any other now.
mt.proposed.adminonly: An admin accepts or deletes it.
mt.proposed.by: by {by} on {at}, from a BOM import. Nothing can be received or taken for it until it is accepted.
mt.proposed.note: {n} articles proposed by an edge wait for an admin.
mt.search: Search name, maker, part number, place
mt.serials: Serial numbers, one per line (or leave empty and give a number)
mt.title: Stock
op.hint: An organisation gets a shared workspace and its first admin, who manages everything else. As an operator you see organisation names and edges, never their content, unless you are a member.
op.name: Organisation name, e.g. Example Workshop
op.needs: Needs a name and the first admin's e-mail.
op.ready: {name} is ready. If you are its admin,
op.sameas.hint: Leave empty for a new organisation. With an organisation's code from another site, this one takes the same ids.
op.title: Operator · new organisation
or.lead: Lines read from an order e-mail on the edge. Scan the parcel at the shelf, pick its line under From order, and check it in: the stock goes up and the line counts as arrived.
ph.email: Your e-mail is filled in there: {email}
ph.hint: Point the phone's camera at this code: it opens Scan there, and you sign in on the phone.
ph.qr: QR code that opens Scan on the phone
ph.title: Scan with the phone
pp.disable.confirm: Disable {email}? They can no longer sign in until you enable the account again.
pp.hint: Every account on this site. There is no sign-up: people come by invitation, from an organisation's admins or from you. A disabled account cannot sign in; its memberships stay.
pp.resent: The invitation to {email} was sent again.
pp.sent: {email} had no account: an invitation is on its way.
pp.title: Operator · people
sc.denied: The camera was not allowed. Allow it for this site, or type the code.
sc.hint: Point the camera at a label of ours, an EAN on a box or a manufacturer's QR; or hold an NFC tag to the phone. A code nobody knows yet can be bound here.
sc.nfcdenied: NFC was not allowed, or is switched off.
sc.nfcunread: That tag could not be read. Try again.
sc.nfcwaiting: Hold the tag to the phone…
sc.nocamera: No camera could be opened here. Type the code instead.
sc.nonfc: This browser cannot read NFC tags (only Chrome on Android can). An iPhone opens our tags by itself: hold it to one.
sc.smallHint: A small label: zoom in and hold the phone a hand's width away, so it can focus.
sc.title: Scan
set.groups.hint: Groups: {groups}. Being added to a group does not change tokens you already hold, so sign out and back in after a change.
set.language.hint: Saved with your account, so it follows you to other devices.
un.alias.code: Scan, type or paste the code (a serial barcode, the maker's QR, a GS1 DataMatrix)
un.alias.hint: A code already on this part opens this card too. A plain EAN names the product: it goes on the article, and asks which unit.
un.bind.missing: The article is not in the catalogue yet?
un.blank: This code belongs to nothing yet. Choose what it is stuck on.
un.flash.name: What, e.g. Raspberry Pi OS Lite
un.install.code: Scan or type the code of the unit it goes into
un.newViaIntake: New article: photos into the intake
un.nfc.done: The tag holds this card's link.
un.nfc.lock: Lock the tag afterwards? A locked tag can never be written again. OK locks it, Cancel leaves it writable.
un.notaunit: That code is not a unit of this organisation.
un.title: Part
un.unknown: Nobody in your organisations knows this code yet. Choose what it belongs to, and it opens that from now on.
un.unknown.product: A product's barcode nobody here knows yet. It names the article, not one item: bind it to the article once, and every box of it is known.
wm.hint: Parts come from the stock of {name}. Reserve puts them aside; used means built in or used up; release gives a reservation back, return gives back what was used.
wm.title: What this workspace took
ws.boxes.none: No box is marked for this workspace yet.
ws.repo.hint: Open: the software and the hardware model go to GitHub. Stock, places, prices and people stay here.
ws.repo.none: Not on GitHub yet. Link it on the edge: Link to GitHub.
